program: Runs the binference engine and talks to it from the terminal.
option.json: Print JSON for scripts instead of text
option.set: Set a config key for this run, written as `key=value`
option.foreground: Run the engine in this terminal until you press Ctrl+C, as the background service runs it
option.lines: How many of the last lines to show
option.follow: Keep showing new lines until you press Ctrl+C
option.agent: The agent's id; the only agent when left out
option.wallet: The wallet's id; the agent's default wallet when left out
option.venues: Every venue a contract call may use, separated by commas, such as kyberswap,okx
option.perTx: The most native coin one contract call may carry, such as 0.5
option.dayCapUsd: The size of every 24-hour cap in US dollars at its floor price, such as 2000
option.agentOrAll: The agent's id; every agent and the install when left out
option.label: A name for the address, such as cold wallet
option.ruleName: The alert's name, shown on the rule's card, 1 to 64 characters
option.ruleToken: The token each alert trades: its symbol, such as CAKE, or its address
option.ruleSide: Whether each alert buys or sells the token
option.ruleUsd: Each fill's size in dollars, such as 20
option.ruleAmount: Each fill's size as an amount, such as 0.5: of what a buy spends, or of the token a sale sells
option.rulePercent: Each fill's size as a percent of the balance, such as 25: of what a buy spends, or of the token a sale sells
option.ruleSpend: What a buy spends: a symbol or an address; the chain's coin when left out
option.ruleWorstPrice: The worst price a fill takes, in dollars per token; no worst price when left out
option.ruleSlippage: The most slippage a fill takes, in percent, such as 0.5; the agent's limit when left out
option.ruleMaxFills: The most fills before the rule ends; no limit when left out
option.ruleRate: The alerts the rule takes in a minute, 1 to 60; 1 when left out
option.ruleTtl: How long the rule lasts, such as 7d, up to 365d; 30 days when left out
option.ruleBefore: Show the alerts older than this one, by the number the list shows
option.addressChain: The chain the address is on, by its name in the registry, such as base-mainnet or solana; BNB Smart Chain when left out
option.walletLabel: A name for the wallet, such as savings
option.identityDescription: A few words about the agent, published on chain for good; 1 to 280 characters
option.launchWallet: Make the agent's launch wallet, the one wallet that trades on a launch's own curve
option.bridgeWallet: Make the agent's bridge wallet, the one wallet that deposits into a bridge whose deposit names no recipient, such as Relay
option.fix: Fix what the check may fix: make files and folders others can open yours alone
option.state: Also remove the state folder: the config, the databases, the keys, the logs and the backups in it
option.webhooks: Also publish the path alert rules receive alerts on to the internet, over Tailscale Funnel; it asks first
option.off: Take off what binference published over Tailscale; everything else Tailscale serves stays
command.start: Start the engine as a background service, which starts again each time you log in
command.status: Show whether the engine runs, its agents and its health signals
command.health: Check that the engine runs and is ready
command.report: Write a support bundle to share: versions, config, checks and the newest log lines, with no secret
command.approval: Show the agent's approval mode, or set it to manual or auto
argument.mode: The approval mode to set: manual or auto
command.live: Switch the agent to live: its trades use real money from its wallet
command.paper: Switch the agent back to paper mode, where nothing is sent on chain
command.confirm: Confirm the card of an intent, as its Confirm button does
command.deny: Cancel the card of an intent, as its Cancel button does
argument.intent: The intent's id, starting with int_
command.wallet: List the agent wallets and show the address to fund
command.walletList: List the agent wallets, each with its label and address
command.walletAddress: Show the address to fund the agent's default wallet at
command.walletCreate: Make a new agent wallet under a ceiling of its own; asks for the owner key
command.walletExport: Show a wallet's private key once, after a warning; asks for the owner key
command.ceiling: Show a wallet's ceiling as custody holds it: its chains, venues, cap, the addresses a send may pay and the 24-hour caps
command.ceilingSet: Change, with the owner key, the venues a contract call may use and the most it may carry on every wallet of the agent, or the 24-hour caps every wallet shares
command.freeze: Freeze every agent and the install, or the agent --agent names: their open cards and unsigned actions are cancelled
command.unfreeze: Open the card that unfreezes every frozen agent, or the agent --agent names; confirming it unfreezes
command.safety: Show what is frozen, the rescue under way and the rescue address
command.safetyStatus: Show what is frozen, the rescue under way and the rescue address
command.telegram: Pair the owner's Telegram bot with another account
command.telegramPair: Make a new link that pairs another Telegram account with the bot; the current owner stays until it is opened
command.console: Make a single-use link that pairs a browser with the console
command.chat: Chat with an agent in the terminal: its answers, cards, questions and notices
command.agent: Commands on one agent: its on-chain identity
command.agentIdentity: Show the agent's on-chain identity, or opt it in with the owner key and open the card that registers it
command.signer: Manage the machines whose agent keys sign for the wallets
command.signerRevoke: Remove a machine's agent key from every wallet; asks for the owner key
command.ownerKey: Make an owner key on a machine with a terminal, for an install set up without one
command.ownerKeyCreate: Make an owner key, show its code once in this terminal, and print its public half
argument.signer: The signer ID: the key quorum of the machine's agent key, as `binference init --attach` printed it
command.address: List, save and remove the addresses a send may pay
command.addressList: List the agent's saved addresses, each with when a send may pay it
command.addressAdd: Save an address a send on its chain, or a bridge to it, may pay, in the address book and the wallets' ceilings; asks for the owner key
command.addressRemove: Remove a saved address: binference sends nothing to it from then on
command.credential: List, store and delete the credentials the agent asks for, which it never sees
command.credentialList: List the stored credentials by name, with the hosts each may be sent to
command.credentialSet: Store a credential, typed at a masked prompt, and the hosts it may be sent to
argument.credential: The credential's name, such as DUNE_API_KEY
option.allowHost: A host the credential may be sent to, such as api.dune.com; repeat for more
credential.count: {count, plural, =0 {No credential is stored.} one {# credential is stored:} other {# credentials are stored:}}
credential.stored: Stored {name}; it may be sent to {hosts}. The agent never sees its value.
credential.deleted: Deleted {name}; it is purged with its value in 30 days.
credential.needsTerminal: A credential's value is typed at a masked prompt, so run this in a terminal without --yes or --json.
command.webhook: Make, list, rotate and delete alert rules: a rule fills on paper inside its bounds each time an alert reaches its URL
command.webhookList: List the alert rules that are active or wait for their card
command.webhookCreate: Make an alert rule with its bounds, show its URL once, then show its card to confirm
command.webhookEvents: List the alerts a rule's URL took and what each became, newest first
command.webhookRotate: Give an alert rule a new URL, shown once; the old one no longer works from then on
command.webhookDelete: Delete an alert rule; its URL no longer works from then on
command.limit: Show the agent's limits in effect, and the looser ones that wait
command.limitSet: Change the agent's limits, each as `key=value`: a stricter one applies at once, a looser one in 24 hours
command.limitCancel: Drop the looser limits that wait; the limits in effect stay
command.config: Show and change the config in config.json5
command.configGet: Show the config as it loads, or one key of it, with every secret shown as its source's kind
command.configSet: Change one config key in config.json5 through the engine, keeping the file's comments
argument.configKey: The config key, its parts joined with dots, such as `engine.port`
argument.configValue: The value, read as JSON5 (7460, true, "text", [1, 2], or null to remove the config key), else as text
option.fromEnv: Set the key to the secret source that reads this environment variable
option.fromKeychain: Set the key to the secret source that reads this keychain entry
option.fromCredential: Set the key to the secret source that reads this credential stored in the engine
configGet.noKey: There is no config key {key}. Run `binference config get` to see every config key.
configSet.restart: It applies after a restart: run `binference restart`.
configSet.oneValue: Give {key} one value: a value, `--from-env` or `--from-keychain`.
configSet.secretSource: {key} takes a secret, which config.json5 never holds as text. Give its source with `--from-env` and the variable's name, or `--from-keychain` and the entry's name.
configSet.badKey: binference cannot read the config key {key}. Join its parts with dots, such as `engine.port`.
argument.limitSets: Each limit as `key=value`, named and in the units `defaults` uses in config.json5, such as limits.perTradeUsd=50
argument.sendAddress: The address as its chain writes it: 0x and 40 hex digits on an EVM chain, base58 on Solana
argument.entry: The address book entry's id, starting with adr_
argument.rule: The alert rule's id, starting with whr_, as `binference webhook list` shows it
command.check: Check this install: its config, who can open its files, its unlock mode and the engine
command.reset: Clear the agents' chats, notes and caches after a sealed backup; wallets, keys, limits, orders and history stay
command.uninstall: Remove binference's background service and the program; with --state, its state folder too
command.expose: Publish the Mini App inside your tailnet over Tailscale, and with --webhooks the path alert rules receive alerts on
usage.invalid: binference cannot read this command line. Run `binference --help` to see the commands and what each one takes.
start.ready: binference is running. The console and the WebSocket are at http://{host}:{port}, the local IPC at {ipc}, and the log at {logFile}. Press Ctrl+C to stop.
start.restarting: binference stopped to restart and starts again now.
start.stoppedLate: binference stopped, but these steps did not finish: {steps}. Run `binference logs` to see why.
start.alreadyRunning: binference already runs on the state folder {folder}. Stop it first, or set BINFERENCE_HOME to another folder.
start.configInvalid: {file} has {count, plural, one {# problem} other {# problems}}. Fix each one, then start again.
start.storeDamaged: The database {file} failed its integrity check. Restore a backup, then start again.
start.backupFailed: binference did not update the database {file}: the backup it takes first failed, because {reason, select, snapshot {the database could not be copied} write {the backup file could not be written; check the disk's free space} check {reading it back found a part that does not match} other {of a fault `binference logs` shows}}. Fix that, then start again.
start.portTaken: Port {port} is in use by another program. Stop that program, or set `engine.port` in config.json5 to a free port.
command.stop: Stop the engine; the background service starts it again when you log in
command.restart: Stop the engine, then start it again as the background service
service.started: binference runs as a background service and starts again each time you log in. Its local IPC is at {ipc}, its log at {logFile} and the service's own output at {serviceLog}.
service.stillStarting: It is still starting; `binference status` shows when it is ready.
service.alreadyRunning: binference already runs as the background service. Run `binference restart` to start it again with this version and these settings.
service.homeMoved: The background service runs on the state folder in your home folder, and BINFERENCE_HOME moves this run to {folder}. Run `binference start --foreground` to run binference on that folder in this terminal.
service.failed: The OS did not start the background service ({code}). Run `binference start --foreground` to run binference in this terminal, or read {serviceLog}.
service.silent: The background service started, but binference did not answer within {seconds} seconds, so the service is stopped until your next login. Read {serviceLog} and run `binference logs` to see why.
stop.serviceKept: binference stopped. The background service starts it again when you log in; `binference start` starts it now.
stop.late: binference still runs on the state folder {folder}. Run `binference logs` to see why it did not stop.
command.service: Manage the background service that starts binference when you log in
command.serviceRemove: Stop binference and remove its background service from this machine; the state folder stays
serviceRemove.removed: binference stopped, and its background service is removed: it no longer starts when you log in. The state folder {folder} stays.
serviceRemove.none: binference is stopped, and this machine has no background service to remove. The state folder {folder} stays.
report.written: The support bundle is at {file}. It holds the versions, the config with each secret shown only by its secret source's kind, the check's findings, the engine's status and the newest log lines, with addresses cut short and each URL shown only by its kind. It holds no secret, address book entry or chat. Read it before you share it.
uninstall.title: binference uninstall
uninstall.plan: binference stops, its background service is removed, then the program. The state folder {folder} stays.
uninstall.planState: binference stops, its background service is removed, then the state folder {folder}, binference's keychain entries and the program.
uninstall.warning: Your wallets and what they hold stay in Privy. Once the state folder is gone, only your owner key moves their tokens: run `binference init --attach` on a machine you set up again, or move everything to your rescue address with `binference rescue` before you uninstall. The owner key is not in the state folder: it is the code binference init showed you once, which you keep offline. The backups in the state folder go with it; copies in backups.copyTo stay.
uninstall.ask: Type {phrase} to go on, or press Ctrl+C to keep binference.
uninstall.needsYes: binference uninstall asks you to type {phrase} first. Run it in a terminal, or add --yes to uninstall without the question.
uninstall.tradeSending: A live trade is being sent. Wait until binference says how it ended, then run binference uninstall --state again.
uninstall.tradeSendingStopped: A live trade was still being sent, so the state folder stays. binference is stopped and its background service is removed. Run binference start --foreground until the trade ends, then run binference uninstall --state again.
uninstall.serviceFailed: The OS did not remove the background service ({code}). Nothing else was removed. Run binference service remove to try again.
uninstall.notStateFolder: {folder} holds no config.json5 and no engine.sqlite, or holds your home folder, so binference did not remove it. The background service is removed.
uninstall.serviceRemoved: binference stopped, and its background service is removed.
uninstall.serviceNone: binference is stopped. This machine had no background service to remove.
uninstall.stateRemoved: {count, plural, =0 {The state folder {folder} is removed.} one {The state folder {folder} is removed, with # keychain entry: {names}.} other {The state folder {folder} is removed, with # keychain entries: {names}.}}
uninstall.agentKeyFolder: The agent key was in the state folder, so it is gone with it.
uninstall.agentKeyKeychainRemoved: The agent key is removed from the OS keychain.
uninstall.agentKeyKeychainLeft: The OS keychain could not remove the agent key, so it stays in it under the service binference, entry agent-key. Remove it in your keychain app: with the Privy app secret it still signs inside the wallets' ceilings.
uninstall.agentKeyCommand: The agent key stays where your unlock command reads it, through {program}; binference cannot remove it there. Remove it in that program, such as your password manager: with the Privy app secret it still signs inside the wallets' ceilings.
uninstall.agentKeyUnknown: config.json5 did not load, so binference cannot say where the agent key was kept. It removed the agent key from the OS keychain if it was there. If your unlock mode was command, the key stays where your command reads it; remove it there.
uninstall.stateKept: The state folder {folder} stays. Run binference uninstall --state to remove it too.
uninstall.programByHand: Windows keeps the files of a program that runs, so remove binference once this command ends: {command}
uninstall.programFailed: npm did not remove the program. Run {command} to remove it.
uninstall.programNotNpm: binference runs from {folder}, which npm did not install, so it stays. Remove it the way you installed it.
uninstall.scriptRemoved: {node, select, yes {The launcher and the Node the install script put in {folder} are removed too.} other {The launcher the install script put in {folder} is removed too.}}
uninstall.scriptFailed: binference could not remove what the install script put in place. Remove it yourself: {command}
uninstall.pathLine: If you added binference's folder to PATH, remove this line from your shell's startup file (such as ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc):
uninstall.pathFolder: If you added {folder} to your user PATH, remove it in "Edit environment variables for your account".
reset.title: binference reset
reset.plan: binference stops and makes a backup sealed to your owner key. Then it clears every agent's chats and notes, the messages waiting for the agent, its open questions and the token risk cache. Your wallets, the link to Privy, the keys, the config, the limits, saved addresses, auto orders, schedules, workspace files and the trade history stay, so the wallets read as before. Then binference starts again as it ran.
reset.ask: Type {phrase} to go on, or press Ctrl+C to keep everything.
reset.needsYes: binference reset asks you to type {phrase} first. Run it in a terminal, or add --yes to reset without the question.
reset.configInvalid: config.json5 does not load, so binference cannot make the backup that comes first. Run binference check to see why, then reset again. Nothing was cleared.
reset.tradeSending: A live trade is being sent. Wait until binference says how it ended, then run binference reset again. Nothing was cleared.
reset.locked: binference started again on {folder} while the reset waited, so nothing was cleared. Run binference reset again.
reset.unreadable: engine.sqlite is missing, does not open, or waits for the engine to update it. Start binference once, then reset again. Nothing was cleared.
reset.updating: An update of binference has not ended, and the copies it keeps would bring the chats back, so nothing was cleared. Run binference update to end it, then reset again.
reset.backupFailed: {failure, select, no_owner_key {This install has no owner key yet, so no backup can be sealed to it.} other {The backup stopped at its {failure} step.}} Nothing was cleared. Run binference backup create to see the backup on its own, then reset again.
reset.done: Backup {backup} is made and checked, at {file}. Cleared: {sessions, plural, one {# chat} other {# chats}} with {events, plural, one {# message} other {# messages}}, {notes, plural, one {# note} other {# notes}}, {inbox, plural, one {# message} other {# messages}} waiting for the agent, {questions, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}} and {riskReports, plural, one {# cached risk report} other {# cached risk reports}}. Your wallets and everything else stay.
config.unreadable: {file} is not valid JSON5 at line {line}, column {column}.
config.newer_version: {file} is version {version}, from a newer binference; this one reads up to version {supported}.
config.older_version: {file} is version {version}; this binference reads version {current}.
config.bad_value: {path} holds a value it does not take (got {got}).
config.bad_value_unseen: {path} holds a value it does not take.
config.bad_key: {path} uses a name that is not valid at that place.
config.secret_inline: {path} holds a secret as plain text.
config.bad_flag: The flag {flag} is not written as `--set key=value`.
configFix.update_binference: Update binference, or restore a backup of {file}.
configFix.remove_key.file: Remove it from {file}, or check its spelling.
configFix.remove_key.flag: Leave out the flag {flag}, or check its spelling.
configFix.change_value.file: Set it in {file} or remove it.
configFix.change_value.env: Set {variable} to a value it takes, or unset it.
configFix.change_value.flag: Change the flag {flag}, or leave it out.
configFix.use_secret_source: Run `binference check --fix` to move it to the keychain, or write a secret source in its place.
connect.notRunning: binference is not running on the state folder {folder}. Start it with `binference start`.
connect.noSignIn: The CLI cannot sign in: {file} is missing. Start binference once with `binference start` to write it.
connect.refused: binference refused the CLI ({code}). Start binference again with `binference start`, so the CLI can sign in again.
connect.failed: binference did not answer ({code}). Run `binference logs` to see why.
status.summary: binference {version} is {state, select, ready {running} starting {starting} locked {running but locked} other {{state}}}, on protocol version {protocol}.
status.agents: {count, plural, =0 {No agents yet.} one {# agent:} other {# agents:}}
status.agent: {id}: {mode, select, paper {paper mode} live {live} other {{mode}}}{frozen, select, yes {, frozen} other {}}
status.autoAsksPlugin: {id}: auto mode asks for every proposal while a community plugin is on
status.signal: {name}: {state, select, ok {ok} warn {needs a look} fail {failing} other {{state}}}
status.signalSince: {name}: {state, select, ok {ok} warn {needs a look} fail {failing} other {{state}}} since {when}
status.signalLag: {name}: {blocks, plural, one {# block} other {# blocks}} behind the chain
status.signalUnpriced: {name}: no price for {count, plural, one {# watched token} other {# watched tokens}}, so their auto orders cannot trigger
status.backupKeyOld: Backups are still sealed to the owner key itself. Enter the owner key code once, in any command that asks for it, and the next backups are sealed to a key of their own.
health.starting: binference is still starting. Try again in a few seconds.
logs.none: There is no log yet at {file}. Start binference with `binference start`.
agent.none: binference has no agent yet. Run `binference init` to make one.
chat.needsTerminal: binference chat needs a terminal on both its input and its output. Run it in a terminal, or chat in Telegram or the console.
chat.pickAgent: Which agent do you want to chat with?
agent.several: binference has {count, plural, one {# agent} other {# agents}}. Name one with `--agent`: {agents}.
approval.current: {agent} is in {mode, select, auto {auto} other {manual}} mode, since {changedAt}.
approval.unchanged: {agent} is in {mode, select, auto {auto} other {manual}} mode already, since {changedAt}.
approval.set: {agent} is in {mode, select, auto {auto} other {manual}} mode now, since {changedAt}.
approval.autoNote: In auto mode, the agent's buys, sells and swaps within its per-trade cap and its 24-hour cap run without a tap, each with a receipt. Sends, buys of a token that is not verified or has a risk warning, and anything over a cap still ask you. Run `binference approval manual` to switch back.
approval.pluginAsks: A community plugin is on, so auto mode asks you for every proposal: the words of its tools reach every turn. Disable it with `binference plugin disable` and its name to let auto mode run.
mode.live: {name} ({agent}) is live now. Its trades use real money from its wallet, and its first live card says so.
mode.paper: {name} ({agent}) is in paper mode now: its trades fill on paper and nothing is sent on chain. Cards already open keep the mode they were proposed in.
mode.fundFirst: Run `binference wallet address` to see the address to fund.
live.wrongPhrase: Type {phrase} to go live, or press Ctrl+C to stay in paper mode.
live.needsTerminal: Going live shows the disclaimer and asks you to type {phrase}. Run `binference live` in a terminal, without --yes or --json.
confirm.paperWaiting: Confirmed {intent}. It fills on paper once binference has a price for what it sells.
confirm.sending: Confirmed {intent}. binference is sending it on chain.
confirm.reopened: The price moved, so binference opened card version {version}: {sold} → at least {bought}. Check it, then run `binference confirm {intent}` again.
confirm.unfrozen: Confirmed {intent}. {scope, select, install {Every agent is unfrozen} other {{agent} is unfrozen}}.
confirm.order: Confirmed {intent}. {state, select, active {The auto order is active.} expired {The auto order did not start: it expired before the confirmation.} cancelled {The auto order did not start: it was cancelled first.} awaiting_confirmation {The auto order did not start: it was cancelled first.} unread {The auto order's state could not be read now.} other {The auto order started.}}
confirm.webhookRule: Confirmed {intent}. {state, select, active {The alert rule is active: its URL takes alerts now, and each fills on paper.} unread {The alert rule's state could not be read now.} other {The alert rule did not start: it was deleted or expired first.}}
confirm.configChanged: Confirmed {intent}. The settings changed; the card's receipt says whether some apply after a restart.
confirm.ask: Confirm this card? Type yes to confirm, or no to leave it open
confirm.notConfirmed: Nothing was confirmed. The card of {intent} stays open until it expires.
confirm.needsTerminal: Confirming shows the card and asks first. Run `binference confirm {intent}` in a terminal, or add --yes to confirm the card without the question.
wallet.count: {count, plural, =0 {No agent wallets yet.} one {# agent wallet:} other {# agent wallets:}}
wallet.item: {label} ({wallet}) of {agent}: {address} on {chain}{role, select, launch {, launch wallet} bridge {, bridge wallet} other {}}{extra, select, yes {, extra: nothing runs from it, rescue what it holds} other {}}{archived, select, yes {, archived} other {}}
wallet.address: To fund {label} ({wallet}), pay into this address on {chain}:
wallet.none: {agent} has no wallet yet. Run `binference init` to make one.
wallet.created: Made {label} ({wallet}) for {agent} on {chain}. Its ceiling lets it trade on the agent's venues and send only to the rescue address and the saved addresses. To fund it, pay into this address:
wallet.createdLaunch: Made the launch wallet {label} ({wallet}) for {agent} on {chain}. Its ceiling lets it trade on launch curves and on the agent's venues, and send only to the rescue address and the saved addresses. Fund it with a small amount from your own wallet: if the agent key is stolen, everything it holds is at risk. To fund it, pay into this address:
wallet.createdBridge: Made the bridge wallet {label} ({wallet}) for {agent} on {chain}. Its ceiling lets it deposit into the bridges that name no recipient, such as Relay, and send only to the rescue address and the saved addresses; it cannot trade. Fund it with a small amount from your own wallet: if the agent key is stolen, everything it holds is at risk. To fund it, pay into this address:
ceiling.heading: The ceiling of {label} ({wallet}), as custody holds it at {readAt}:
ceiling.venues: {count, plural, =0 {Venues: none, so no contract call is allowed} other {Venues: {venues}}}
ceiling.cap: One contract call may carry at most {amount} {symbol}.
ceiling.capBase: One contract call may carry at most {amount} of the native coin, in base units.
ceiling.recipients: {count, plural, =0 {A send may pay no address.} one {A send may pay # address:} other {A send may pay # addresses:}}
ceiling.dayCaps: {count, plural, =0 {No 24-hour caps.} other {24-hour caps, which every wallet shares:}}
ceiling.dayCapSent: {amount} {symbol} sent per {hours, number} hours, {usd} at the floor price
ceiling.dayCapApproved: {amount} {symbol} approved per {hours, number} hours, {usd} at the floor price
ceiling.dayCapBase: {amount} base units of {asset} per {hours, number} hours, {usd} at the floor price
ceiling.launchCalls: As a launch wallet, it may also call {calls} on any contract, under the cap and the 24-hour caps above: a stolen key can take what it holds.

ceiling.dayCapsEveryWallet: This changes the 24-hour caps of every wallet of every agent, as they share them.
ceiling.changed: The ceilings changed. Every surface announces it.
walletExport.warningTitle: Before the private key is shown
walletExport.warning: Anyone with this private key controls every token in the wallet {address}, on every chain, with none of binference's limits, ceiling or rescue address. Never paste it into a website, a chat or a cloud note, and keep it out of screenshots. binference shows it once and keeps no copy.
walletExport.ask: Type the last 4 characters of the wallet's address to show its private key

check.ceilingPromise: What the ceiling promises: even with this machine's keys, no one can send to an address you did not save, call a contract or approve a spender no enabled venue declares, or lose more through trades than its 24-hour caps. Inside those caps, a trade can still fill at a bad price. A launch wallet, if you made one, is an exception: its ceiling allows launch calls on any contract and approvals of any spender, so a stolen key can take what it holds. Keep in it only what curve trades need. A bridge wallet, if you made one, is the other: a Relay deposit pays whoever its order names, so a stolen key can take what it holds. Keep in it only what the next bridge needs.

mcpSetup.change: {part, select, token {Client token} server {MCP server entry} other {Skill}} {action, select, created {made} updated {updated} unchanged {unchanged} removed {removed} other {not there}}: {path}
mcpSetup.plan: {part, select, token {Client token} server {MCP server entry} other {Skill}} {action, select, created {would be made} updated {would be updated} unchanged {stays unchanged} removed {would be removed} other {is not there}}: {path}
mcpSetup.done: {client} is set up. Start a new {client} session to load the binference tools and skill; every proposal waits for your tap in Telegram or the console.
mcpSetup.removed: {client} no longer has the binference tools, the skill or a client token.
mcpSetup.expires: The client token works until {at}. Run the setup again to make a new one.
mcpSetup.dryRun: Nothing was changed. Run the same command without `--dry-run` to make these changes.
mcpSetup.noSkill: This binference has no bundled binference-tools skill, so nothing was set up. Install binference again.
mcpSetup.skillLint: The bundled skill tells the agent to ask for a secret at line {line}, so nothing was set up. Install binference again.
mcpSetup.unreadable: {file} could not be read as the client writes it, so it was left as it is. Fix the file, then run the setup again.
mcpSetup.claudeFailed: `claude mcp` failed, so the MCP server entry was not changed. Run `claude mcp list` to check Claude Code, then run the setup again.
command.mcpSession: Start Claude Code or Codex once with the binference tools and a client token that ends with the session
option.mcpSessionClient: The MCP client to start: claude-code or codex
option.mcpSessionTtl: How long the session's client token works: 30m, 2h or 1d, at most 24h; 1h when left out
option.printConfig: Print the config and the client token for a client you start yourself, and start nothing
mcpSession.started: {client} starts with the binference tools. Its client token works until {at} and is revoked when {client} exits.
mcpSession.codexServers: Codex also loads the other MCP servers in its config.toml.
mcpSession.noClient: `{program}` is not on PATH, so {client} did not start. Install {client}, or start it yourself with `--print-config`.
mcpSession.revoked: The session's client token is revoked.
mcpSession.revokeFailed: The session's client token could not be revoked, so it works until {at}. Revoke it sooner by starting the engine and running `binference mcp setup` again.
mcpSession.printClaude: Save this config to a file, set {variable} to the value on the last line in Claude Code's environment, and start it with `claude --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config` and the file's path. The client token works until {at}; nothing revokes it before then.
mcpSession.printCodex: Set {variable} to the value on the last line in Codex's environment, and start Codex with this command. The client token works until {at}; nothing revokes it before then.
command.plugin: Add, list, enable, disable and remove community plugins
command.pluginAdd: Add a community plugin from npm, or update one, after its permission review
command.pluginDisable: Disable an installed plugin at once
command.pluginRemove: Remove an installed plugin and its data
argument.pluginSource: the plugin's npm package at an exact version, such as npm:fear-index@1.2.0
argument.pluginName: the plugin's name, as `binference plugin list` shows it
option.pluginHash: the version's npm integrity (sha512-...); read from npm when left out
option.pluginName: the plugin's name, typed for a plugin without npm provenance
plugin.badSource: Name the plugin as npm:package@version, an exact version, such as npm:fear-index@1.2.0.
plugin.hashUnread: npm did not answer with this version's integrity. Check the name and version, or give it with --hash.
plugin.needsYes: This plugin waits for your review. Run the command in a terminal, or add --yes after reading the review with --json.
plugin.needsName: This plugin has no npm provenance. Run the command in a terminal and type its name, or add --name {plugin}.
plugin.wrongName: That is not this plugin's name, so nothing was added.
plugin.added: {plugin} {version} is added and on. Its tools reach the agent from its next turn.
plugin.addedOff: {plugin} {version} is added and stays off. Enable it with `binference plugin enable {plugin}`.
plugin.count: {count, plural, =0 {No community plugins yet. Add one with `binference plugin add npm:package@version`.} one {# community plugin:} other {# community plugins:}}
plugin.item: {plugin} {version}: {state, select, enabled {on} other {off}}{reason, select, owner {, disabled by you} crashes {, stopped after crashing} changed {, its files changed} other {}} · npm provenance {provenance, select, verified {checked} other {none}} · tools: {tools}
plugin.notInstalled: No installed plugin is named {plugin}. `binference plugin list` shows them.
plugin.enabled: {plugin} is on. Its tools reach the agent from its next turn.
plugin.disabled: {plugin} is off. The agent can no longer call its tools.
plugin.stillRunning: The install still runs. `binference plugin list` shows the plugin once it is added.
plugin.engineStopped: binference stopped before the install ended. Start it, then add the plugin again.
command.update: Install a newer binference release from npm, check it, and put the old one back if its check fails
option.updateTo: The release to install, such as 2026.11.0; the newest on updates.channel when left out
update.image: binference runs in its Docker image here, which never updates in place. Pull the image of the newer release and start a new container from it on the same state folder.
update.notNpm: binference runs from {folder}, which npm did not install, so update leaves it as it is. Update that copy the way you made it.
update.configInvalid: config.json5 does not load, so binference cannot update. Run binference check to see why, then update again. Nothing changed.
update.proxyHeld: The proxy config.json5 names cannot be read, so binference reaches nothing and nothing changed. Run binference check to see why.
update.badVersion: {version} is not a binference release; name one such as 2026.11.0 or 2026.11.0-beta.1. Nothing changed.
update.notNewer: binference {current} runs here, and {version} is not newer, so nothing changed.
update.upToDate: binference {current} is the newest release on the {channel} channel.
update.windows: binference update does not run on Windows yet, since Windows keeps the running program's files open. To install binference {version}, run binference stop, then npm install --global binference@{version}, then binference start. Nothing changed.
update.running: Another binference update is running on this state folder, so nothing changed. Let it finish, then run binference update again if you still need to.
update.interrupted: The update stopped on a fault ({code}). Run binference update again: it ends what this run left, and puts the old version back if the update did not finish.
update.recordUnread: updates/state.json, which an earlier update left, does not read, so binference changed nothing and its engine stays locked. Run binference logs to see how that update ended, then binference report to ask for help.
update.unfinishedNotNpm: An earlier update did not finish, and binference runs here from a folder npm did not install, so this command cannot end it. Run binference update from the npm install that started it.
update.undoStopped: binference {version} is not undone yet: {reason, select, foreground {binference runs in the foreground of another terminal; stop it there, then run binference update again} late {its engine did not stop in time; run binference stop, then binference update again} held {an engine started on the state folder; run binference stop, then binference update again} npm {npm could not put {previous} back; run {command}, then binference update again} tarball {the copy of {previous} it kept is gone; run {command}, then binference update again} copies {the copies of your records it kept are missing or changed, so they cannot go back; restore backup {backup} with binference backup restore} other {{reason}}}. Until then the engine stays locked and signs nothing.
update.notStarted: binference did not start again. Run binference logs to see why, then binference start.
update.registryUnreachable: npm's registry could not be read, so nothing changed. Check this machine's network or proxy, then try again.
update.downloadFailed: binference {version} cannot be installed: {reason, select, not_published {npm holds no such release} registry_unreachable {npm's registry could not be read} hash_mismatch {its package is not the one npm's record names} provenance_failed {its npm provenance does not show binference's own release build} other {{reason}}}. Nothing changed.
update.busy: A live trade is on its way, so nothing changed. Run binference update again once it is done.
update.foreground: binference runs in the foreground of another terminal, where update cannot start it again. Stop it there, run binference update, then start it again. Nothing changed.
update.locked: binference started again while the update waited, so nothing changed. Run binference update again.
update.unreadable: engine.sqlite does not open as this binference reads it, so nothing changed. Run binference check to see why.
update.backupFailed: {failure, select, no_owner_key {This install has no owner key yet, so no backup can be sealed to it.} other {The backup before the update stopped at its {failure} step.}} Nothing changed. Run binference backup create to see the backup on its own, then update again.
update.installing: Backup {backup} is made. Installing binference {version}. If this stops part way, run binference update again to put {previous} back; if binference does not run at all, run {command} first.
update.done: binference is now {version}, in place of {previous}.{started, select, no { Its engine was stopped and stays stopped; its first start runs any change the new version makes to your records, so watch binference start.} starting { Its engine is still starting; binference status shows when it is ready.} other {}}
update.rolledBack: binference {version} {failed, select, checks {failed the check {checks}} install {could not be installed by npm} start {did not start as itself, locked while it was checked} unread {printed no check binference could read} unfinished {was left part way by an earlier update} restart {did not start again as it should after its check} interrupted {stopped on a fault} other {failed}}, so binference went back to {previous}. Your records and config.json5 are as they were before the update; messages and alerts that came while it was checked are not kept.{started, select, no { Start binference with binference start.} other {}}
command.skill: Review the skills the agent proposes and the workspace skills that wait for you
command.skillProposals: List the agent's skill proposals and its waiting workspace skills
command.skillShow: Show a skill proposal whole: its scan findings and its changes
command.skillApply: Apply a skill proposal, after you read it
command.skillAccept: Accept a waiting workspace skill as its files are now
option.skillAll: list the applied, rejected and stale proposals too
option.skillReason: why, in a line the agent reads at its next turn
skill.count: {count, plural, =0 {No skill proposal.} one {# skill proposal:} other {# skill proposals:}}
skill.item: {proposal}: {kind, select, create {new skill} other {change to}} "{name}", {status}{findings, plural, =0 {} one {, # scan finding} other {, # scan findings}}: {description}
skill.waitingCount: {count, plural, =0 {Every workspace skill loads.} one {# workspace skill waits for you:} other {# workspace skills wait for you:}}

skill.head: {kind, select, create {New skill} other {Change to skill}} "{name}" ({status}): {description}
